caller_review.NativeMlKem: ExpandMatrix divides/mods only its public k=0..8 counter. BigInteger carries fixed3/9 reference-array initialization indices or public array lengths. Select uses only literal56 for its wide shift.
caller_review.NativePolynomial: Stage, block, coefficient and twiddle-table indices control all division, table selection and allocation; coefficients enter only the verified native field operations.
caller_review.NativeKeccak/NativeShake: Rate, phase, position, input/output lengths, fixed25/5 arrays and public rotation-offset tables control metadata helpers. Payload lanes enter only bv64 shifts with public distances.
caller_review.NativeCodec/NativeSampling: Widths, grouping indices and lengths are public; component operand-stack data-flow guards check PublicDiv/PublicMod/Extract/Shift boundaries. Decode(m,1) validates secret message bits, but decoded d1/d4/d10 values are bounded by1/15/1023, so IsCanonical outcomes are constant. Only d12 validation can vary; its KEM caller parses public encoded keys. Feed validates the empty/public prefix and rejects public rho-derived matrix candidates; CBD payloads avoid those branches.
caller_review.allocation/tuple/result: TypeDescriptor allocation/fill dispatch uses public dimensions/type descriptors and fixed zero values. Tuple2 and Result constructors/getters retain references. No owned KEM call reaches IntegerRange, payload toString/hashCode or mutable metadata writes.
caller_review.boundary: Generated constructors, mutable arrays and metadata are internal; the production facade must keep them inaccessible to callers. This review is source/runtime discipline, not a JVM timing theorem.
